name: batch-13
prompt:
Create ONE production game-icon SPRITE ATLAS, exactly 3 columns by 3 rows on a square canvas, ideally 2048x2048, genuinely TRANSPARENT alpha PNG. Input image is the user's approved style sheet, STYLE reference only. Match that soft tactile dimensional 3D collectible family: gentle warm upper-left diffuse studio light, rounded yet faithful forms, bright pastel/candy color, subtle ambient occlusion, restrained material detail. Each object's true material remains recognizable: paper, wood, glass, metal, woven cloth. No same-clay treatment on everything. No heavy dark outlines or flat vector art.

CRITICAL PACKAGING: There are EXACTLY NINE equal square virtual cells in a regular 3x3 grid. Draw ONE specified object/group centered within EACH virtual cell, at ONLY 48–52% of cell width/height, with at least 24% EMPTY TRANSPARENT MARGIN ON EVERY SIDE. Nothing may touch a virtual cell edge or cross into a neighbor. All strings, handles, leaves and shadows stay inside their own cell. Think SMALL MINIATURE ICONS with LARGE EMPTY GUTTERS, NOT large illustrations filling the sheet. Icon centers are x=16.67%,50%,83.33%, y=16.67%,50%,83.33% of the image. Each icon must fit in a box 18% of the overall image size. Empty space between shapes is essential. No visible grid lines, no backgrounds, no color squares, no borders, no captions, numbers, words, ID labels, titles or decorative props. Empty padding is genuine alpha transparency, NOT a drawn checkerboard. Top-left through bottom-right order is mandatory; do not swap cells. Each tile will be cropped at exact one-third boundaries into a separate icon. Keep centered and similarly weighted, readable at 32–66px. All objects fully in frame, no cropping. Only allow inscription glyphs explicitly specified in subject. Do not invent sacred symbols, cultural ornament, claims or text. No extra humans/hands/landscape/pedestals. Subject list in strict row-major order:
1. Cell row 1, column 1: Seven flat painted wooden tangram pieces fitted into one square: five triangles of three sizes, one square and one parallelogram. Use coral, ochre, teal, blue, lavender, pale blue and dusty rose; keep the seven seams clear and add no markings.
2. Cell row 1, column 2: A pale bamboo-and-wood double-wheel diabolo with teal wheel rims, small coral accents and one narrow brown axle, balanced on a fine tan string between two brown hand sticks. Keep the two hollow wheel forms distinct rather than making a solid ball.
3. Cell row 1, column 3: A pale mint cloth game board with dark teal connecting lines and cream circular stations, one blue round playing token, and four separate half-round tan wooden throwing sticks below it. Preserve the board-and-four-sticks grouping without adding opponents or extra tokens.
4. Cell row 2, column 1: Two painted wooden nesting dolls of different sizes: a large teal doll with a coral headscarf, cream face and simple flower apron, beside a smaller sage-green doll with a cream face and ochre flower. Keep their rounded bodies, flat bases and the larger doll's horizontal opening seam.
5. Cell row 2, column 2: A natural honey-colored wooden cup-and-ball toy with a narrow upright spike, a horizontal crosspiece carrying unequal side cups and a red ball on a thin grey-brown string. The ball has one cream stripe; keep the cups concave and the tether attached.
6. Cell row 2, column 3: A small open brown wooden spinning-wheel frame with a large spoked wheel, a smaller horizontal metal spindle to its left and a fine connecting drive cord. A cream cotton tuft sits beside the spindle; preserve the exposed wheel, belt and spindle relationship.
7. Cell row 3, column 1: A painted wooden nutcracker figure with a natural-tan face, dark top hat and boots, muted-green coat, cream pointed beard and a rear wooden lever. One brown walnut sits beside it; keep the hinged lower jaw evident and add no regalia or lettering.
8. Cell row 3, column 2: A tall honey-brown wooden chocolate whisk standing in a terracotta handled cup filled with dark chocolate. Preserve its fluted lower head and two loose wooden rings near the surface, with only a few pale tan foam bubbles.
9. Cell row 3, column 3: A small rounded rectangular warm-brown wooden thumb-piano board with five silver-blue metal tongues of varied lengths, secured by two horizontal bridge bars. Keep the five separate tongues and the two small pale metal loops near the bottom corners; no added ornament.
